problems.title: Translate “three times as large” into an equation
problems.question: For which value of $x$ is $4x-2$ three times $8-3x$?
problems.idea: Write the first expression as three times the second, then solve.
formulas: $A$ is three times $B$ means $A=3B$.
Adding the same quantity to both sides preserves an equation.
steps: Add $9x+2$ to both sides: $13x=26$.
Divide by $13$: $x=2$. Check: the expressions are $6$ and $2$, and $6=3\cdot2$.

problems.title: Reverse the digits of a two-digit number
problems.question: The digits of a two-digit number add to $9$. Adding $27$ reverses the digits. Find the number.
problems.idea: Represent the number using its tens and units digits.
formulas: A two-digit number with tens digit $a$ and units digit $b$ is $10a+b$.
steps: The digit sum gives $a+b=9$.
Reversal after adding $27$ gives $10a+b+27=10b+a$. Thus $9(b-a)=27$, so $b-a=3$.
Add $a+b=9$ and $b-a=3$: $2b=12$, giving $b=6$ and $a=3$.
The number is $36$; indeed $36+27=63$.

problems.title: Two bags of sugar
problems.question: Two bags initially contain $50$ kg of sugar each. Three times as much sugar is removed from one bag as from the other. The first then contains half as much as the second. How much remains in each?
problems.idea: Let the smaller amount removed be $x$ kg; the other amount removed is $3x$ kg.
formulas: Remaining amount $=$ initial amount $-$ amount removed.
steps: The remaining amounts are $50-3x$ and $50-x$.
The first is half the second: $2(50-3x)=50-x$.
The bags contain $50-30=20$ kg and $50-10=40$ kg. These are in the required ratio $1:2$.

problems.title: Add work rates
problems.question: One worker completes a job in $6$ hours, another in $8$ hours. What fraction do they complete together in $2$ hours?
problems.idea: Add fractions of the job completed per hour, then multiply by time.
formulas: Work rate $=1/\text{time for the whole job}$.
Work completed $=(r_1+r_2)t$.
steps: The hourly rates are $1/6$ and $1/8$ of the job.
Together they complete $1/6+1/8=4/24+3/24=7/24$ per hour.
In $2$ hours they complete $2\cdot7/24=7/12$ of the job.

problems.title: From time per kilometre to speed
problems.question: A car travels at $60$ km/h and covers each kilometre half a minute faster than a second car. Find the second car’s speed in km/min.
problems.idea: Convert the known speed first, then compare the times needed for one kilometre.
formulas: $t=d/v$ and $v=d/t$.
$1$ hour $=60$ minutes.
steps: $60$ km/h is $1$ km/min, so the first car takes $1$ minute per kilometre.
The second takes $1+0.5=1.5$ minutes per kilometre.
Its speed is $1/1.5=2/3$ km/min, equal to $40$ km/h.

problems.title: Find the values of an expression from factored roots
problems.question: If $(x-5)(x+3)=0$, what values can $x-5$ take?
problems.idea: First solve for $x$, then evaluate the requested expression for every root.
formulas: $uv=0$ implies $u=0$ or $v=0$.
steps: From $x-5=0$, obtain $x=5$, which gives $x-5=0$.
From $x+3=0$, obtain $x=-3$, which gives $x-5=-8$.

problems.title: Use a known solution to find a parameter
problems.question: One solution of $(2x+1)^2=b-4$ is $x=2$. Find $b$.
problems.idea: A solution must make both sides equal when substituted.
formulas: If $x=c$ solves an equation, substitute $c$ for every occurrence of $x$.
steps: Substitute $x=2$: $(2\cdot2+1)^2=b-4$.
The square is $5^2=25$, so $25=b-4$.

problems.title: Distances covered before two cars meet
problems.question: Two cars start at the same time from different cities and travel towards each other. The first is $1.5$ times as fast as the second and has covered $600$ km when they meet. Find the distance between the cities.
problems.idea: Equal travel times make the distances proportional to the speeds.
formulas: $d=vt$; for equal $t$, $d_1/d_2=v_1/v_2$.
Total distance between starting points $=d_1+d_2$.
steps: The distance ratio is $d_1/d_2=1.5$.
The second car travels $600/1.5=400$ km.
The distance between the cities is $600+400=1000$ km.

problems.title: Solve a linear equation with fractions
problems.question: Solve $7-x-\frac19(4x+6)=6-\frac{15x+3}{12}$.
problems.idea: Multiply the entire equation by a common denominator so no fractions remain.
formulas: The least common multiple of $9$ and $12$ is $36$.
Multiply every term on both sides by the same nonzero number.
steps: Collect terms: $228-52x=207-45x$, so $21=7x$ and $x=3$.
Check at $x=3$: both original sides equal $2$.

problems.title: A ratio of differences of squares
problems.question: Evaluate $\dfrac{10001^2-9999^2}{199^2+2\cdot199+1}$.
problems.idea: Factor the numerator and recognise a perfect square in the denominator.
steps: The denominator is $(199+1)^2=200^2=40000$.
The quotient is $40000/40000=1$.

problems.title: When a linear equation has no solution
problems.question: For which value of $a$ does $(a^2-9)x=a+3$ have no solution?
problems.idea:
An equation $cx=d$ has no solution precisely when $c=0$ but $d
e0$.
formulas: $0x=d$ is impossible for $d\ne0$, and is true for every $x$ when $d=0$.
steps: The coefficient of $x$ is zero only for $a=3$ or $a=-3$.
At $a=3$, the equation is $0x=6$, which is impossible.
At $a=-3$, it is $0x=0$, which has every real number as a solution.
For other $a$, the nonzero coefficient gives a unique solution.

problems.title: Product of roots using factorisation
problems.question: Find the product of the roots of $4(x-3)^2-9(2x+1)^2=0$.
problems.idea: The expression is a difference of squares, so it factors into two linear expressions.
formulas: A zero product has at least one zero factor.
steps: The roots are $x=-9/4$ and $x=3/8$.
Their product is $(-9/4)(3/8)=-27/32$.

problems.title: Drying apples preserves the dry material
problems.question: Fresh apples are $72\%$ water; dried apples are $20\%$ water. How much dried fruit can be made from $30$ kg of fresh apples?
problems.idea: Only water is removed. The mass of the non-water material stays the same.
formulas: Dry-material mass $=\text{total mass}\times(1-\text{water fraction})$.
steps: Fresh apples contain $28\%$ dry material, weighing $30\cdot0.28=8.4$ kg.
Dried apples contain $80\%$ dry material. If their mass is $m$, then $0.80m=8.4$.
problems.answer: $10.5$ kg (option დ), assuming only water is lost.

problems.title: Distance from a chord midpoint to a diameter
problems.question: A chord crosses a diameter at $30^\circ$ and is divided there into lengths $10$ cm and $14$ cm. Find the perpendicular distance from the chord’s midpoint to the diameter.
problems.idea: The chord is $24$ cm long, so its midpoint is $2$ cm from the crossing point.
formulas: Midpoint distance from an end $=\frac12\times\text{segment length}$.
In a right triangle, the side opposite $30^\circ$ is half the hypotenuse.
steps: Call the crossing point $P$ and the chord midpoint $M$. The whole chord has length $10+14=24$ cm.
$M$ is $12$ cm from either end, so $PM=|12-10|=2$ cm.
Drop a perpendicular $MH$ to the diameter. Triangle $PMH$ is right-angled at $H$, and its angle at $P$ is $30^\circ$.
Therefore $MH=PM/2=1$ cm.

problems.title: Two workers with rates in a 2:1 ratio
problems.question: Two workers together complete a job in $10$ days. One works twice as fast as the other. Find the time each would need alone.
problems.idea: Use a rate $r$ for the slower worker and $2r$ for the faster worker.
formulas: Rate $=1/\text{completion time}$; combined rates add.
steps: Together they work at rate $r+2r=3r=1/10$ of the job per day.
Thus $r=1/30$. The slower worker needs $30$ days alone.
The faster worker’s rate is $2/30=1/15$, so that worker needs $15$ days.

problems.title: A tangent parallel to a diameter
problems.question: A point $P$ on a circle is $3$ cm from a tangent line and $4$ cm from a diameter parallel to that tangent. Find the circle’s diameter.
problems.idea: The distance between the parallel tangent and central diameter is the radius.
formulas: A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent.
Diameter $=2R$.
For a point between two parallel lines, its perpendicular distances to them add to the distance between the lines.
steps: The point cannot lie beyond the central diameter on the far side: then its distance to the tangent would exceed its distance to the diameter, contrary to $3<4$.
It lies between the tangent and the parallel central diameter. Their separation is therefore $3+4=7$ cm.
That separation equals the radius $R$, so the diameter is $2\cdot7=14$ cm.
problems.note: The printed choices list $14$ cm twice (ბ and ვ). Both labels represent the same numerical answer.

problems.title: The centre of an inscribed circle
problems.question: Which triangle lines meet at the centre of its inscribed circle?
problems.idea: The centre must be equally distant from all three sides.
formulas: A point on an angle bisector is equally distant from the two sides of that angle.
The incenter is the intersection of the internal angle bisectors.
steps: The circle is tangent to all three sides, so the perpendicular distance from its centre to each side is its radius.
Equal distances to the two sides at a vertex place the centre on that vertex’s internal angle bisector.
Applying this at the vertices identifies the intersection of the internal angle bisectors.

problems.title: Two perpendicular chords
problems.question: Two perpendicular chords intersect. Each chord is divided into parts $3$ cm and $7$ cm. Find the distance from the circle’s centre to each chord.
problems.idea: The centre lies on each chord’s perpendicular bisector.
formulas: Half a chord of length $3+7$ is $5$ cm.
The perpendicular bisector of every chord passes through the centre.
steps: Let the chord intersection be $P$, with the two chord lines as perpendicular coordinate axes.
On either chord, its midpoint is $|5-3|=2$ cm from $P$.
The perpendicular bisector of the horizontal chord is a vertical line $2$ cm from $P$; the perpendicular bisector of the vertical chord is a horizontal line $2$ cm from $P$.
Their intersection is the circle’s centre. Its perpendicular distance to either chord line is $2$ cm.

problems.title: Three tangent circles
problems.question: Two equal small circles touch each other and internally touch a larger circle. The triangle joining the three centres has perimeter $30$ cm. Find the larger radius.
problems.idea: Tangency translates the distances between centres into sums or differences of radii.
formulas: External tangency: centre distance $=r_1+r_2$.
Internal tangency: centre distance $=R-r$.
steps: Write $R$ for the large radius and $r$ for either small radius.
The two small centres are $2r$ apart. Each is $R-r$ from the large centre.
The triangle’s perimeter is $2r+(R-r)+(R-r)=2R$.
Thus $2R=30$, so $R=15$ cm.

problems.title: A chord subtending a 60-degree central angle
problems.question: A $27$ cm segment crosses a circle, dividing the segment into consecutive parts in the ratio $2:3:4$. The middle part is a chord subtending $60^\circ$ at the centre. Find the circle’s diameter.
problems.idea: Find the chord length from the ratio. The two radii and this chord form an equilateral triangle.
formulas: One ratio unit $=\text{total}/\text{sum of ratio parts}$.
An isosceles triangle with vertex angle $60^\circ$ is equilateral.
Diameter $=2R$.
steps: The ratio has $2+3+4=9$ units, so each unit is $27/9=3$ cm.
The middle part has length $3\cdot3=9$ cm; this is the chord inside the circle.
The two radii to its endpoints are equal and enclose $60^\circ$. The other two angles are also $60^\circ$, so the chord equals the radius.
Thus $R=9$ cm and the diameter is $18$ cm.

problems.title: Compare common tangent segments
problems.question: Two circles touch externally at $A$. In the diagram, $BK$ and $MN$ are common external tangents, and the tangent at $A$ meets them at $P$ and $T$. Compare $BK$ and $PT$.
problems.idea: Tangent segments from the same external point are equal; the diagram is symmetric across the line of centres.
formulas: Tangents from one point to the same circle have equal lengths.
Reflection across the line of two circle centres preserves both circles and exchanges the two common external tangents.
steps: From point $P$, tangency to the left circle gives $PB=PA$; tangency to the right gives $PK=PA$.
Since $P$ lies between $B$ and $K$, $BK=BP+PK=2PA$.
Reflection in the line of centres exchanges $P$ and $T$ while fixing $A$, hence $PA=AT$.
Therefore $PT=PA+AT=2PA=BK$.

problems.title: An angle between tangents equals its minor arc
problems.question: Two tangents from an external point form angle $A$. The minor arc between their points of contact has the same degree measure as $A$. Find $A$.
problems.idea: The angle between two tangents is supplementary to the central angle over the minor arc.
formulas: Tangent angle $=180^\circ-\text{minor-arc measure}$.
steps: Let both the tangent angle and the minor arc have measure $x$ degrees.
The tangent-angle rule gives $x=180-x$.
Thus $2x=180$ and $x=90$.

problems.title: A remainder after polynomial division
problems.question: Find the remainder when $3x^4-9x^3+7x-3$ is divided by $x^2-3x-2$.
problems.idea: A quadratic divisor leaves a remainder of degree at most one. Replace $x^2$ by $3x+2$ when computing that remainder.
formulas: Modulo $x^2-3x-2$, $x^2\equiv3x+2$.
Equal remainders may be added and multiplied before reduction.
steps: $x^3\equiv x(3x+2)=3x^2+2x\equiv11x+6$.
Substitute these remainders: $3(39x+22)-9(11x+6)+7x-3$.
Collect coefficients: $(117-99+7)x+(66-54-3)=25x+9$.
The result is linear, so no further division by the quadratic is needed.

problems.title: A tangent and a diameter in the diagram
problems.question: In the diagram, $AB$ is tangent at $B$, and line $AK$ passes through the circle’s centre $O$ with $K$ the nearer circle intersection. If $\angle A=37^\circ$, find minor arc $BK$.
problems.idea: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at its contact point.
formulas: $OB\perp AB$.
Triangle angles add to $180^\circ$.
A minor arc has the same degree measure as its central angle.
steps: Triangle $AOB$ has a right angle at $B$ and angle $37^\circ$ at $A$.
Therefore $\angle AOB=180^\circ-90^\circ-37^\circ=53^\circ$.
Rays $OA$ and $OK$ point in the same direction, so $\angle BOK=53^\circ$.
The minor arc $BK$ consequently measures $53^\circ$.
problems.note: The diagram for this question is positioned higher on the source page, beside earlier questions. Its line through $K$ and $O$ supplies the needed diameter information.

problems.title: What intersecting circles tell us about centre distance
problems.question: Two circles with radii $10$ cm and $17$ cm intersect in two points. Can their centre distance be determined?
problems.idea: For two proper intersections, the centre distance is between the difference and sum of the radii.
formulas: $|R-r|<d<R+r$ for two circles intersecting in two points.
steps: The lower bound is $|17-10|=7$ cm; the upper bound is $17+10=27$ cm.
Thus any distance strictly between $7$ and $27$ cm can occur.
For example, both $12$ cm and $25$ cm satisfy the condition. The given radii do not determine a unique distance.
problems.answer: It cannot be uniquely determined (option ვ); the range is $7<d<27$ cm.
problems.note: If the question were asking which listed distances are possible, both $12$ cm and $25$ cm would be possible. The printed wording asks what the distance is, so “cannot determine” is the appropriate single choice.
